title: Power Apps: Dataverse custom APIs in generative pages
summary: Hold: the telemetry setup notes omit the Azure-resource permissions needed in addition to the Power Platform and Dataverse administrator roles. The claim that this moves generative pages from displaying data to triggering business operations also misstates the existing capability: Microsoft says row operations already trigger plug-ins.

claims.claim: The capability is user-opt-in: a maker chooses to add and use a custom API in the page.
claims.quote:
To use a custom API:

1. In the generative page designer, select **Add** > **Custom API**.
2. Select a custom API from the current environment.

claims.claim: Dataverse plug-in code can run as another user.
claims.quote: Sometimes you need the code in a plug-in to run in the context of a different user, for example to perform an operation on their behalf.

claims.claim: Generative pages are solution-aware.
claims.quote: Generative pages are solution-aware and can be added to a solution (via an app) to facilitate moving between environments.

claims.claim: This moves generative pages from displaying data to triggering business operations.
claims.quote: This capability is different from a plug-in that runs automatically when a Dataverse row is created, updated, or deleted. Those plug-ins already run when a generative page performs the corresponding data operation and don't need to be added to the page.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence of Why it matters with 'This adds an explicit way for generative pages to invoke named server-side business operations.' The cited feature page distinguishes explicit custom API invocation from plug-ins already triggered by page data operations.

claims.claim: How custom API calls from generative pages appear in auditing remains undocumented.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" "custom API" "audit". Read generative-pages and returned external-tools and dataApi excerpts; telemetry is documented, but no feature-specific custom API audit representation was found.

claims.claim: The low cost rating reflects known implementation effort and the maker experience's lack of additional AI or message credits.
claims.quote: No, the maker experience for generative pages (and plans) don't require any additional AI or message credits.
claims.fix: Append 'Licensing specific to custom API calls from generative pages is not yet published.' to the cost rationale. The assessment scale requires this qualification when a low rating describes known indirect costs while feature-specific licensing remains unpublished.
